title: Fast and slow pointers
objective: Detect a loop in a linked list with two pointers moving at different speeds.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Cycle detection (Floyd's tortoise and hare)

simplifies: This only says whether there is a loop. Floyd's method can also find where the loop starts, with one more pass; that part is left out.

quiz.prompt: If the list has no loop, what happens?

options.text: fast reaches the end (None) and it returns False
options.explanation: Right. Falling off the end proves the list ends.

options.text: slow and fast meet at the last node
options.explanation: They only meet inside a loop. Without one, fast simply runs out of list.
The loop condition checks fast and fast.next, so it stops at the end.

quiz.prompt: Inside a loop, why can't fast keep jumping over slow forever?

options.text: Each pass, fast gains exactly one step on slow, so the gap shrinks by one until it is zero
options.explanation: Right. A gap that shrinks by exactly one each time must reach zero, so they land on the same node.
Being faster is why it catches up, but the exact one-step gain is why it can't skip past.
Length doesn't matter: any gap shrinks by one per pass.
